doc: This file is a DIFFERENT oracle from the physical sstabledump JSONL goldens
(`*-Data.db.jsonl`). The physical goldens enumerate every on-disk cell —
INCLUDING tombstones, deleted rows, and expired-but-uncompacted TTL cells.
Row-count/value parity against a physical dump therefore CANNOT catch a
read-time-reconciliation bug: when CQLite fails to reconcile, both sides still
contain the shadowed/expired rows and parity passes while a real Cassandra
SELECT diverges (issue #1741, the read-path P0 this oracle guards against
Each case below records the POST-RECONCILIATION result set a real Cassandra
`SELECT` returns for a canonical query, evaluated at a PINNED `now`
(`pinned_now_secs`, epoch seconds) so TTL expiry is deterministic and never
wall-clock-flaky. The reader honors the pin via the debug-only
`physical_row_count` is the count of `type == "row"` entries in the committed
sstabledump golden — an anti-empty-pass sanity check AND (where it exceeds
`expected_rows.len()`) a direct demonstration of the physical-vs-semantic gap

note: All three fixtures below are REAL Apache Cassandra 5.0.2 SSTables committed
to the repo (test-data/datasets/sstables/test_compaction_tombstone_ttl/**),
with provenance already tracked in test-data/cassandra-parity-manifest.yml
(scenarios cass.compaction.*shadow_row_delete / *ttl_expired_live /
*rt_cross_gen). They are post-major-compaction (nb-3-big) fixtures and still
present the physical-vs-semantic divergence (a physical dump enumerates the
surviving row/RT/expired markers that a SELECT hides).
GAP (issue #1742 AC2): a dedicated SINGLE-generation (pre-compaction) fixture
carrying coexisting partition-deletion + older LIVE rows, a range tombstone
with a LIVE row INSIDE its bounds, and an expired TTL cell whose VALUE is
still on disk requires generating uncompacted SSTables from a live Cassandra
container (autocompaction disabled, single flush). Docker/Cassandra was not
available in the implementing sandbox, so no such fixture is added here.
Tracked for real-Cassandra regeneration in the issue #1742 follow-up.

cases.pinned_now_note: 2026-07-01T23:56:40Z — AFTER row ck=1's TTL expiry (expires_at 2026-07-01T23:54:23Z, epoch 1782950063); row ck=2 has no TTL so it stays live at any now.
No TTL in this fixture; pin is fixed for determinism only. Row (id=1, ck=1) is a ROW tombstone (no live cells) and must be hidden.

No TTL; pin fixed for determinism. A range tombstone covers clustering [10,25]; the live rows sit at ck=5 and ck=30 (OUTSIDE the RT), so both survive — this pins that the RT open/close markers are skipped and do not wrongly shadow rows outside their bounds. A LIVE-row-INSIDE-RT case needs the single-gen fixture noted in provenance.gap.

cases.query: SELECT pk, ck FROM test_da.wide_table WHERE pk = 1 AND ck >= 100 AND ck < 110
cases.pinned_now_note: 2027-01-15T08:00:00Z. This fixture carries no TTL, tombstone or deletion of any kind (every row is unconditionally live at any now), so the pin only removes wall-clock nondeterminism from the lane; it never selects between rows.
note: Issue #3002 (BTI Rows.db row-index root base + leading OSS50 NEXT_COMPONENT).
A BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVATION oracle for the BTI clustering-slice read path
(`scan_single_partition_clustering` -> `resolve_clustering_seek_window` ->
`bti_clustering_row_window`): the two compensating defects cancelled on this
fixture, so the semantic result set must be IDENTICAL before and after removing
the compensation. A change here is a regression, not a semantic update.
Oracle derivation: test_da/wide_table is a real Apache Cassandra 5.0 `da` (BTI)
SSTable whose committed sstabledump golden (da-2-bti-Data.db.jsonl) holds 900
physical rows (3 partitions x ck=0..299) with NO tombstone/TTL/deletion marker,
so physical == semantic here: the expected result set is exactly the golden's
pk=1 rows with 100 <= ck < 110, read off the golden rather than hand-authored.
flight_lane=false: the Flight `do_get` ticket surface is a whole-table projection
scan with no WHERE clause, so a partition + clustering-slice query is not
expressible on that lane (see cqlite-flight/tests/query_semantics_flight_parity.rs).

cases.query: SELECT pk, ck, row_col FROM test_tomb.static_with_tombstones WHERE pk = 1 AND ck >= 3
cases.pinned_now_note: 2026-07-01T23:56:40Z (the same pin the sibling cases use). This fixture carries NO TTL of any kind, so no row's visibility depends on `now` — the pin only removes wall-clock nondeterminism. The tombstones' localDeletionTimes (2026-06-24T22:59:06Z) govern GC purge, never read visibility, so they do not interact with the pin either.
note: Issue #3094: a DELETED CELL must read as NULL, never surface a raw tombstone.
THE CELL-TOMBSTONE SHAPE ON CASSANDRA-WRITTEN BYTES. test_tomb
static_with_tombstones is a real Apache Cassandra 5.0 `nb` SSTable (single
flush), committed to the repo with provenance in
test-data/cassandra-parity-manifest.yml. Its committed sstabledump golden
(nb-1-big-Data.db.jsonl) enumerates, in partition pk=1:
* ck=1 - live liveness marker + live row_col='row_1'
* ck=2 - a ROW DELETION (marked_deleted 2021-01-02), zero cells
* ck=3 - a LIVE liveness marker (tstamp 2021-01-01) whose ONLY regular
cell, row_col, is a SIMPLE CELL TOMBSTONE (tstamp 2021-01-02)
* a RANGE TOMBSTONE bound pair covering [ck=4, ck=5] (marked_deleted
2021-01-02); no data rows lie inside it in this fixture
* ck=6 - live liveness marker + live row_col='row_6'
Cassandra semantics (Cell.isLive / Row liveness in UnfilteredSerializer):
ck=2 is deleted outright, while ck=3 SURVIVES because its primary-key
liveness marker is live and its deleted row_col is simply ABSENT from the
reconciled row - which CQL renders as NULL. So the SELECT returns 3 rows,
one of them with row_col = null, while the physical dump shows 4 `type:
row` entries.
This is exactly the divergence a physical-dump oracle CANNOT catch: the
golden enumerates the cell tombstone, so parity against it stays green
while a real SELECT diverges. Before #3094 the deleted cell reached the row
carrier as Value::Tombstone(CellTombstone) and the fail-closed Arrow
encoder (#1485) errored the WHOLE Flight do_get stream.
SCOPE OF THE QUERY (why `WHERE pk = 1 AND ck >= 3`, and why stat_col is
not projected). This table declares a STATIC column, and the static read
shape is a separate, tracked divergence (see BypassReason::StaticColumns
and the issue #3058 differential). Concretely, on the single-generation
read path `merge_static_cells` injects the live stat_col into the
ROW-TOMBSTONED ck=2 before `build_display_row` runs, so `has_data_cell`
is true, the row is emitted as data instead of a filtered tombstone
MARKER, and ck=2 wrongly surfaces as an all-null row. That is an
independent defect of the static-injection path, NOT of cell-tombstone
reconciliation, and is tracked as issue #3121, so this case bounds its
clustering slice to ck >= 3 to own the CELL-TOMBSTONE property only and
never to encode that other divergence as expected behaviour. Widening the
slice to ck >= 2 is #3121's acceptance evidence, not this case's.
The bound keeps a LIVE control row
(ck=6, row_col='row_6') in the same result set, so the ck=3 null cannot
pass vacuously as a blanket loss of row_col.
flight_lane=false: the Flight `do_get` ticket surface is a whole-table
projection scan with no WHERE clause, so this bounded slice is not
expressible on that lane. The Flight `do_get` arms for this property are
covered instead by cqlite-flight/tests/issue_3094_cell_tombstone_null.rs
(both forced arms) and by the re-enabled ck=5 cell-tombstone shape in
cqlite-flight/tests/issue_3058_forced_path_differential.rs.
